decisions.title: Installed host release and catch-up baseline
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1—revert one baseline record. Bottom line: host 0.84.2 is already installed; record this review as the new baseline. Project fit: `extensions/work-catch-up-baseline.json` still recorded 0.84.1 and `package.json` intentionally accepts the host peer dependency. Upstream evidence: the installed package manifest is 0.84.2 and its changelog documents the release. Benefit: prevents repeat review and preserves decisions. Cost/risk: none beyond release-regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt the baseline record after owner verification.
decisions.verification: Installed @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent is 0.84.2; node scripts/verify-package.mjs passed against the release

decisions.title: Experimental strict sampling for native tools
decisions.rationale: Grade: Trial. Reversibility: Tier 1—unset one environment variable. Bottom line: trial native strict sampling for built-in read/bash/edit/write; do not make it a project default yet. Project fit: ce-workflow relies on native edit/write and already protects its custom tools with strict schemas. Upstream evidence: the captured 0.84.1-to-0.84.2 artifact adds experimental preferred JSON-schema sampling to the four built-ins and confirms the `PI_EXPERIMENTAL=1` gate. Benefit: may reduce malformed native-tool arguments. Cost/risk: explicitly experimental provider/schema behavior. Confidence: medium. Recommendation: run one non-production work item first; retain current default unless it is clean.

decisions.title: Replace the custom strict-tool wrapper
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1. Bottom line: retain registerConstrainedTool. Verified project fit: it normalizes nullable custom-tool parameters and wraps verifier, goal, and mutation tools under tested contracts. Upstream evidence: native experimental sampling applies only to built-in read, bash, edit, and write and does not normalize custom schemas. Benefit: avoids breaking custom tool contracts. Cost/risk: retains a small tested adapter. Confidence: high. Recommendation: do not simplify this code.

decisions.title: Expand templates in generated internal handoffs
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1. Bottom line: preserve sendUserMessage expandPromptTemplates=false for generated protocol messages. Verified project fit: autonomous-goal and role follow-ups are fully materialized and recognized through lifecycle markers. Upstream evidence: 0.84.2 adds an explicit opt-in that dispatches commands and expands skills/templates. Benefit: deterministic internal handoffs. Cost/risk: generated prompts intentionally skip expansion. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local change.

decisions.title: Host provider, TUI, runtime, and sendMessage fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit provider/runtime fixes, fullscreen and startup improvements, streaming-usage repair, default tools, and triggerTurn:false behavior without local adapters. Verified project fit: ce-workflow has no sendMessage call site or JSON streaming consumer and already uses agent_end to agent_settled lifecycle boundaries. Upstream evidence: the 0.84.2 changelog and captured diff place these changes in host-owned surfaces. Benefit: avoids duplicating canonical host behavior. Cost/risk: none beyond package regression risk. Confidence: high. Recommendation: inherit with no local code.

decisions.title: Verified private workflow generation
decisions.rationale: The official stable release is translated into the complete private nine-workflow generation with no ordinary CE runtime surface.

decisions.title: Async workflow reliability and control release
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 (package rollback and one baseline record). Bottom line: adopt the already-installed 0.52.0 release with no ce-workflow runtime shim. Verified project fit: ce-workflow already uses supported async workflowScript launches, pi-subagents steering RPC, durable status files, contact_supervisor, and session-scoped transcript artifacts; repository searches found no removed chain/checkpoint/prompts.render API usage. Verified upstream evidence: the 0.50.0→0.52.0 artifact and installed CHANGELOG add stable-key runs.steer, safer Windows status persistence, correct paused-child/supervisor reconciliation, idle-parent attention wakes, model/context fixes, and bounded host inspection. The new inspection command is RPC-only, while ce-workflow Fleet is a TUI reading trusted local artifacts, so replacing Fleet would not fit. Benefit: safer recovery and control on ce-workflow’s current paths. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure; no source change beyond the catch-up ledger. Confidence: high. Recommendation: Adopt now, verify the existing Fleet/subagent integration, and record 0.52.0.
decisions.verification: Installed pi-subagents package manifest is 0.52.0; node scripts/test-work-fleet.mjs passed

decisions.title: Replace TUI Fleet transcript reads with host inspection RPC
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: keep ce-workflow Fleet's bounded trusted-file transcript reader. Verified project fit: `extensions/work-fleet.js` renders live transcript events inside Pi's TUI and already validates artifact roots. Verified upstream evidence: `/subagents-inspect-rpc` emits its bounded reply only on RPC surfaces and explicitly directs interactive TUI users to package-native status/transcript views. Benefit: avoids adding an RPC host bridge that cannot serve the current TUI surface. Cost/risk: the small local transcript adapter remains. Confidence: high. Recommendation: do not replace Fleet with this RPC-only protocol.

decisions.title: Package-owned runner, model, storage, UI, and lifecycle fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit stable-key workflow steering, external-job providers, status-write resilience, attention wakes, model resolution, storage cleanup, Fleet, and supervisor lifecycle fixes without local adapters. Verified project fit: ce-workflow consumes public workflowScript, RPC steering, status, and artifact boundaries and does not use the removed legacy chain or checkpoint surfaces. Verified upstream evidence: the reviewed 0.51.0 and 0.52.0 changelogs, public docs, tool schema, and captured diff place these behaviors inside pi-subagents. Benefit: keeps ce-workflow smaller while receiving upstream reliability fixes. Cost/risk: normal package regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: inherit with no local source change.

decisions.title: Responsive decision UI and Herdr attention signaling
decisions.rationale: Responsive list layouts and blocked/waiting attention signals are implemented inside pi-ask-user and inherited by ce-workflow's existing ask_user calls. Local dialog policy remains separate and no compatibility shim is required.

decisions.title: ask_user telemetry integration
decisions.rationale: The release exposes no stable per-call telemetry API, while ce-workflow already records tool timing and dialog decisions. Local wrapping would duplicate package behavior without measurable savings; revisit if a public metrics hook appears.

decisions.title: Exact delivery and durable supervisor coordination release
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 (package rollback and one baseline record). Bottom line: adopt the already-installed 0.11.0 release with no ce-workflow runtime shim. Verified project fit: ce-workflow’s autonomous-role policy already requires exact session IDs for trust-sensitive replies, checks pending asks plus run/work-item state, treats timeout as non-cancellation, and uses explicit supersedes/retryOf semantics. Verified upstream evidence: the 0.10.1→0.11.0 artifact and installed public schema add endpoint epochs and exact-send negotiation, durable pending-ask records, idempotent delivery replay, structured delivery outcomes, tmux-pane presence, and broker-owned cancellation/supersession diagnostics. The public intercom tool performs exact target resolution internally, so ce-workflow needs no new targeting adapter. Benefit: prevents stale-name/rebound delivery and makes delayed supervisor coordination safer. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure; no source change beyond the catch-up ledger. Confidence: high. Recommendation: Adopt now, verify ce-workflow’s existing supervisor policy, and record 0.11.0.
decisions.verification: Installed pi-intercom package manifest is 0.11.0; focused buildWorkGoalSystemPrompt supervisor-policy assertions passed

decisions.title: Automated intercom retries or a local exact-send wrapper
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: do not add an automatic retry or endpoint-epoch wrapper around the public intercom tool. Verified project fit: ce-workflow coordinates through agent-visible tool calls and already requires a new authored retry, exact pending-state checks, and explicit cancellation/supersession semantics. Verified upstream evidence: 0.11.0 resolves exact endpoints inside the public tool client, returns outcomeKnown/retryable delivery details, and deliberately never retries authored messages automatically. Benefit: avoids duplicate supervisor instructions and a second delivery owner. Cost/risk: agents must continue making explicit retry decisions. Confidence: high. Recommendation: retain the current policy and consume package-owned exact delivery.

decisions.title: Broker persistence, receipts, presence, and UI details
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit pending-ask persistence, delivery replay records, endpoint epochs, tmux-pane presence, and receipt rendering without ce-workflow adapters. Verified project fit: ce-workflow declares intercom as an optional peer and owns policy text, not broker storage, routing, presence, or tool rendering. Verified upstream evidence: the captured diff and installed public implementation place these behaviors in pi-intercom's broker, client, types, and tool surface. Benefit: safer coordination without duplicate infrastructure. Cost/risk: normal package regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local action.

decisions.title: Removal of the experimental ordered-goal queue
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit pi-goal's removal of its experimental ordered-goal queue without ce-workflow migration code. Verified project fit: repository-wide searches find no pi-goal command, queue setting, event-channel, or tool call site; ce-workflow sequencing is owned by native work items, action leases, and one autonomous objective. Verified upstream evidence: the 0.51.0→0.52.1 artifact and installed README remove queue commands/state/UI, retain inert legacy-state warnings, and keep the package's single-goal tools and managed-run protocol. Benefit: no local compatibility burden and no duplicate queue owner. Cost/risk: none beyond normal package regression exposure for users who independently load pi-goal. Confidence: high. Recommendation: record no local action.

decisions.title: Replace ce-workflow autonomous goals with pi-goal
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 3 after state and command migration. Bottom line: pi-goal 0.52.1 is a single-objective loop, not a substitute for ce-workflow's work-item, lease, verifier, compaction, catch-up, and completion-gate behavior. Verified project fit: `extensions/work-models.js` validates native target state before completion and exposes distinct `work_goal_complete` and `work_goal_human_decision` tools; package.json does not depend on pi-goal. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.52.1 manifest and README expose generic `/goal`, `goal_complete`, `goal_blocked`, `goal_wait`, and a default-off session-local managed-run protocol. Benefit: avoids deleting required domain gates for superficial code reduction. Cost/risk: the existing purpose-built autonomous engine remains. Confidence: high. Recommendation: do not replace ce-workflow goals with pi-goal.

decisions.title: Diagnostics, navigation, and subagent-efficiency release
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 (package rollback/baseline-only record). Bottom line: adopt the already-installed 4.0.1 release and its package-owned diagnostics/navigation improvements without changing ce-workflow role allowlists. Verified project fit: ce-workflow already uses `project_report` only in an availability-gated background verifier and uses native read/grep plus focused LSP checks elsewhere; no repository call site hardcodes the v4-renamed `filePath` tool argument. Verified upstream evidence: the 3.8.74→4.0.1 changelog, public tool schemas, docs, package manifest, and captured diff add always-active `symbol_search`/`module_report`/`read_symbol`/`read_enclosing`, deferred activation for situational AST/LSP tools, subagent light mode, more honest diagnostic coverage, safer read/edit guards, and numerous scanner/LSP correctness fixes. Benefit: faster, lower-context discovery and safer diagnostics are inherited automatically in Pi sessions and subagents. Cost/risk: normal package regression exposure; putting optional pi-lens tools into every ce-workflow agent allowlist would make role launch depend on an optional ambient extension, while the isolated verifier must not read live files through symbol tools. Confidence: high. Recommendation: Adopt now as a package-owned capability release; keep the current optional, availability-gated integration boundary.
decisions.verification: Installed pi-lens package manifest is 4.0.1; node scripts/test-work-start-finish.mjs passed the availability-gated project_report selection and isolated-verifier boundaries; primary LSP diagnostics were clean for extensions/work-models.js and extensions/work-fleet.js

decisions.title: Add optional pi-lens tools to every durable role allowlist
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: do not make worker, planner, reviewer, fixer, or debugger launch depend on optional ambient pi-lens tools. Verified project fit: each role has an explicit required-tool allowlist, while only `work-background-verifier-lens` is selected after a coded `project_report` availability check. Upstream evidence: pi-lens 4.0.1 registers six always-active discovery/diagnostic tools and five situational tools behind `pi_lens_activate_tools`; pi-subagents passes an agent's explicit tool names as required child tools. Benefit: preserves role availability when pi-lens is absent while installed sessions still inherit package guidance and per-edit diagnostics. Cost/risk: roles use native targeted reads rather than forcing the lower-context symbol funnel. Confidence: high. Recommendation: retain the optional integration boundary until pi-lens becomes a declared required dependency.

decisions.title: Use live symbol reads inside immutable checkpoint verification
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: keep checkpoint findings verified through `work_verifier_*` tools, not `module_report`, `read_symbol`, or `read_enclosing`. Verified project fit: the lens verifier treats `project_report` only as hostile orientation and validates every finding against immutable checkpoint-scoped content. Upstream evidence: the new symbol tools read the active workspace and record live read-guard coverage, not ce-workflow's checkpoint. Benefit: avoids time-of-check/time-of-use drift and scope escape. Cost/risk: bounded checkpoint reads remain somewhat less token-efficient. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no verifier tool expansion.

decisions.title: Tool-schema rename, dynamic activation, scanners, LSP, and runtime fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit v4's `path`/`paths` schema, deferred situational-tool loading, subagent light mode, diagnostic honesty, scanner coverage, read guards, graph maintenance, and runtime/UI fixes without ce-workflow adapters. Verified project fit: repository code does not invoke pi-lens tool schemas programmatically and consumes only the stable availability check plus package-owned tool results. Upstream evidence: these changes are implemented and documented within pi-lens 4.0.1. Benefit: avoids duplicating package internals. Cost/risk: normal upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local action.
